# See the traffic Google Analytics misses
Run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 to measure website traffic when visitors reject consent.

Where GA4 loses visibility

GA4 can use persistent identifiers. Simple Analytics calculates session starts without creating visitor identities.

## Where GA4 loses visibility
When analytics consent is denied, Basic Consent Mode blocks Google tags. Advanced Consent Mode can send cookieless pings. Eligible properties can use behavioral modeling for users and sessions in supported reports.

**Measure traffic without relying on Consent Mode modeling.** Simple Analytics gives you an independent, observed dataset to compare with GA4, even when visitors reject consent.

 [How sessions without consent work →](/sessions-without-consent)

## Add a cookieless layer to GA4.
GA4 still runs your reporting, audiences, and conversion workflows. Simple Analytics adds the cookieless baseline, so analysts can see what GA4 reports alongside independently recorded pageviews and events.

### Google Analytics
Identifier-based analysis

Users and sessionsAttribution

User journeys and attribution using available identifiers. Consent and reporting settings affect the results.

+

### Simple Analytics
Observed pageviews and events

Independent baselineNo visitor IDs

Records pageviews and events without visitor IDs. Calculates session starts from pageview context.

=

### Combined
Two measurement methods

Independent baselineCompare trends

Compare matching metrics and investigate differences. The two tools use different session definitions.

### Compare it on your own website
Run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 with a free 30-day proof of concept.

[Book a demo](/demo)

## Send missing traffic data into your own systems
Use Simple Analytics as the cookieless collection layer behind the reporting tools your team already trusts. Send observed traffic into BI, dashboards, warehouses, or your own internal systems.

### API and exports
Pull observed pageviews, events, referrers, and campaign data into your own workflows.

### BI tools
Compare Simple Analytics with GA4 in Looker Studio, Power BI, or internal dashboards.

### Data warehouse
Join cookieless traffic data with your warehouse models without relying on another dashboard.

[Browse integrations](/integrations)[Read the API docs](/api)

### What we do
- Measure pageviews, events, referrers, and campaign parameters without identifying visitors.
- Derive country-level location without storing IP addresses.
- Report cookieless traffic that GA4 cannot fully observe after consent is rejected.

### What we don't
- No cookies, localStorage, or similar browser storage.
- No IP address collection or storage.
- No visitor IDs, user profiles, or cross-site identifiers.
- No cross-session or cross-device tracking.

That makes us compliant with all the major privacy laws out of the box. Read more about [GDPR compliance](/gdpr-compliance), [security](/security), and [privacy-first web analytics](/web-analytics).

## Trusted by teams that need a clearer picture
Simple Analytics helps analysts in [agencies](/use-cases/agencies), [enterprise teams](/use-cases/enterprise), and [white-label partners](/use-cases/white-label) recover visibility into pageviews, clicks, events, and campaign traffic lost through consent banners, blockers, and privacy restrictions.

[How to cancel my account](/cancel-account) - [How to delete my account](/delete-account) # How to add our script Download PDF Include these two lines on every page at the end of your `` (or anywhere else): ``` ``` > To install the script on Wordpress, Ghost, WIX, Squarespace, Webflow, Gatsby, Vue, Django, Ruby, and others, go to [Install on other platforms](/install-on-other-platforms). We have a website setup wizard to test if you installed your script correctly. If you still have problems installing it, please let us know! We helped a lot of people with setting up their script and we love to help you as well. Just [contact](https://simpleanalytics.com/contact) us. ## Server-side tracking We support server-side tracking, [read more about it here](/events/server-side#page-view-data-structure). ## Non-JavaScript environments While most people browse the internet with JavaScript enabled, there are still some users who disable it, fully aware that many websites may not function as intended. If you want to capture data from these visitors, consider adding our `noscript` tag. Be aware that this may also increase traffic from bots, as some don’t have JavaScript enabled. ``` ``` ## Developers With Simple Analytics you don’t need to manually trigger page views in SPA. We automatically trigger page views in [*Single Page Apps* (SPA’s)](/trigger-custom-page-views) like React, Vue, and Angular. You can also use [hash navigation](/hash-mode) to trigger page views. Some people like a very light script. All our scripts are heavily compressed and we have [an extra light](/light) version. If you want to run the script on localhost, please use our dev (`https://scripts.simpleanalyticscdn.com/latest.dev.js`) version. Note the `.dev` part. You might want to [overwrite your hostname](/overwrite-domain-name) from localhost to something like `dev.example.com` (where `example.com` is your domain) to receive it in your dashboard. Make sure to remove the `.dev` part from the script on production. We drop data from some shared preview and proxy domains, like `*.vercel.app`, `*.lovable.app`, and `*.translate.goog`, unless that exact hostname is added to your dashboard. To collect data on such a domain, add the hostname to your dashboard or [overwrite the hostname](/overwrite-domain-name). When you are done implementing [go to your dashboard](https://simpleanalytics.com/websites). If you encounter issues, don’t hesitate to contact us via [our support channels](https://simpleanalytics.com/contact). ### Javascript version If you can’t embed HTML, but you can embed JavaScript, here is the code you need to install Simple Analytics with just JavaScript. ``` // Simple Analytics - 100% privacy-first analytics const script = document.createElement("script"); script.setAttribute("src", "https://scripts.simpleanalyticscdn.com/latest.js"); document.head.appendChild(script); ``` ### Settings via JavaScript Instead of `data-` attributes, you can pass settings with a `window.sa_settings` object. Define it before the script loads. Settings in this object take precedence over `data-` attributes. ``` ``` These settings are available: | Setting | Same as | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | `hostname` | [`data-hostname`](/overwrite-domain-name) | `"example.com"` | | `mode` | [`data-mode`](/hash-mode) | `"hash"` | | `collectDnt` | [`data-collect-dnt`](/dnt) | `true` | | `autoCollect` | [`data-auto-collect`](/trigger-custom-page-views#use-custom-collection-anyway) | `false` | | `ignorePages` | [`data-ignore-pages`](/ignore-pages) | `["/search/*", "/vouchers"]` | | `ignoreMetrics` | [`data-ignore-metrics`](/ignore-metrics) | `["timeonpage", "scrolled"]` | | `allowParams` | [`data-allow-params`](/allow-params) | `["product-id"]` | | `nonUniqueHostnames` | [`data-non-unique-hostnames`](/non-unique-hostnames) | `["checkout.stripe.com"]` | | `strictUtm` | [`data-strict-utm`](/strict-utms) | `true` | | `namespace` | [`data-namespace`](/events#the-variable-sa_event-is-already-used) | `"ba"` | | `pathOverwriter` | [`data-path-overwriter`](/overwrite-path) | `"myPathOverwriter"` | | `metadataCollector` | [`data-metadata-collector`](/metadata) | `"myAddMetadataFunction"` | | `pings` | [`data-pings`](/pings) | `[5, 30, 60]` | | `detect404` | [`data-detect-404`](/events/inline#404-pages) | `true` | | `referrer` | [`data-referrer`](/overwrite-referrer) | `"https://example.com/"` | For `pathOverwriter` and `metadataCollector`, use the name of a function on `window`, not the function itself. The script logs the settings it received in the browser console. ## Browser support We test our script on a wide range of browsers and real devices with [BrowserStack](https://www.browserstack.com/). We support browser, OS, and device versions that their vendors still maintain, and we keep testing them for two years after their end of life. Older browser versions with more than 0.1% global usage stay covered. ## Open source Our user facing scripts are [open source on GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/scripts).

# Install Simple Analytics on other platforms
Download PDF

## Platform guides
We try to make installing Simple Analytics as simple as possible. We want privacy to be accessible as possible. We don’t require the need for a developer if you use any of the following tools.

Read our guides on how to install Simple Analytics on:

- [Google Tag Manager](/install-simple-analytics-with-google-tag-manager) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/google-tag-manager#readme))
- [Wordpress](/install-simple-analytics-on-wordpress) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/wordpress-plugin#readme))
- [Ghost](/install-simple-analytics-on-ghost)
- [WIX](/install-simple-analytics-on-wix)
- [Squarespace](/install-simple-analytics-on-squarespace)
- [Webflow](/install-simple-analytics-on-webflow)
- [Jimdo Creator](/install-simple-analytics-on-jimdo-creator)
- [MailerLite](/install-simple-analytics-on-mailerlite)
- [GoDaddy](/install-simple-analytics-on-godaddy)
- [Netlify](https://app.netlify.com/extensions/simpleanalytics)

Cloudflare has deprecated Cloudflare Apps, so you can no longer install our [Cloudflare App](/install-simple-analytics-on-cloudflare). Add [our script](/script) to your website instead.

> Are you missing your favorite platform? [Let us know!](https://simpleanalytics.com/contact) Happy to create a guide or plugin for you.

## Framework plugins
For most frameworks, you can include the script. We magically track page views, so you don’t have to change your app code. [Read on how we do that](/trigger-custom-page-views). For some, we got requests to create a plugin for them.

Get our official plugins for these frameworks:

- [React](/install-simple-analytics-with-react) (package on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@simpleanalytics/react))
- [Ruby on Rails](/install-simple-analytics-with-ruby-on-rails) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/rubyonrails-plugin#readme))
- [Gatsby](/install-simple-analytics-with-gatsby) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/gatsby-plugin#readme))
- [Vue](/install-simple-analytics-with-vue) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/vue-plugin#readme))
- [VuePress](/install-simple-analytics-with-vuepress) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/vuepress-plugin#readme))
- [Nuxt.js](/install-simple-analytics-with-nuxt) (package on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@simpleanalytics/nuxt))
- [Gridsome](/install-simple-analytics-with-gridsome) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/gridsome-plugin#readme))
- [Django](/install-simple-analytics-with-django) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/simpleanalytics/django-plugin#readme))
- [Analytics library](/install-simple-analytics-via-analytics-package) (source on [GitHub](https://github.com/DavidWells/analytics/tree/master/packages/analytics-plugin-simple-analytics))
- [Hugo](/install-simple-analytics-with-hugo) (guide only)

body.content: # Install Simple Analytics Image of Iron Brands Published on Nov 23, 2023 and edited on Dec 11, 2023 by Iron Brands This guide will outline the steps to install Simple Analytics on your website, including advanced settings like [custom domains](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/bypass-ad-blockers) and DNS settings. It requires some technical knowledge, but we’ll explain it in steps. If you use a website platform, such as [Squarespace](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/install-simple-analytics-on-squarespace), [Webflow](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/install-simple-analytics-on-webflow), [Wix](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/install-simple-analytics-on-wix) or [Google Tag Manager](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/install-simple-analytics-with-google-tag-manager), etc. We have created different guides for those. 1. [Adding your website](#adding-your-website) 2. [Advanced settings](#advanced-settings) 1. [Domains & Statistics](#domains--statistics) 2. [Public Website](#public-website) 3. [Custom Domain](#custom-domain) 4. [DNT](#dnt) 5. [Get help from your team](#get-help-from-your-team) 3. [Adding the script](#adding-the-script) 1. [DNS settings for Custom Domain](#dns-settings-for-custom-domain) Michelin chose Simple Analytics[Join them](/signup) In this guide we'll focus on the standard method suitable for most websites. ## Adding your website The first step is to go to your website's overview. We display five websites here, but yours is probably empty. install-website-overview.png Click "Add website" and enter the domain name or website name. For the sake of this example, we will add *demo.simpleanalytics.com*. install-domain-name.png You can remove *"https"* or *"www"* and enter the root domain. If you have both subdomains and root domains, you can add those separately. Simple Analytics treats subdomains the same as a standalone website. ## Advanced settings Simple Analytics offers several advanced settings you can tweak based on your needs. ### Domains & Statistics Here, you can specify the subdomain you want to track. Each subdomain is treated as a separate website. Although you don't pay extra for each additional website, there is a limit on the number of websites you can add to your plan. In the example, we added the subdomain *demo.simple.analytics.com*. ### Public Website When you want to make your website visitor insights public, you just tick the box. There is also an option to hide certain pages from the public. intall-public-stats.png For example, our website insights are made public, so when you visit *simpleanalytics.com/simpleanalytics.com*, you will see our website stats. ### Custom Domain Another option available is a custom domain, essentially an extra subdomain. If your website is *example.com*, you can add *stats.dot.example.com*, which redirects to your statistics. The primary reason to use a custom domain is to bypass ad blockers. There is also an option to block your office IP addresses, which allows you to prevent certain IP addresses or a range from being counted towards your statistics. By doing this, your visits will not be included in the dashboard, making tracking traffic more accurate. The bypass blocker option is helpful, but its significance is lower than one may think. Although a considerable amount of people use ad blockers, it usually ranges between 2% to 10%, depending on the audience. The percentage for e-commerce websites is likely lower as most users don't use ad blockers. However, if you want to ensure that you can bypass them anyway, you can activate the custom domain option by clicking on it. In the example below, we used *simple.demo.simpleanalytics.com.* But it can be literally anything. install-custom-domain.png ### DNT One option to consider is not tracking visitors, which some browsers allow users to request. However, this feature is no longer supported in many browsers and is gradually fading away. Despite this, Simple Analytics has always respected this feature and has not tracked visitors who opt out. However, users can still collect information from visitors who opt out of tracking, as Simple Analytics does not collect personal data from its visitors. The script will be adjusted accordingly if users click the "do not track visits" option. ### Get help from your team If you feel uncomfortable installing the script on your website, you can invite others to do it for you. By entering their email address, you can grant them access to your account so that they can add the website and update the script on your behalf. This is a useful feature for those who may not have the technical expertise or prefer to delegate these tasks to other team members. install-dev-support.png ## Adding the script Once you have completed the advanced settings, install the Simple Analytics script on your website. Simple Analytics detects the technologies used by your website and provides an HTML code that you can copy and paste into your website. You can also choose from other install options that cover most of the platforms and frameworks out there. install-add-website.png We will scan your website to see what website technologies you use. This might take some time. Once the tool has completed its scan, you will see a few options for installing the script on your website. In this case, it detects two technologies. One option always is to select HTML, the basic language used to create websites. You can also click the "show all" option to see all the available installation options for most platforms and frameworks. You can always let us know if you need additional options, and we will add them. If you encounter any issues with the installation, you can reach out to Simple Analytics for [support](https://simpleanalytics.com/contact). Community support is available for the free plan users, while paid plan users can email Simple Analytics directly for assistance. Let's see what HTML looks like. Include these two lines at the end of your `` (or anywhere else): ``` ``` To add the Simple Analytics script to your website, you must add a few lines of code to your HTML. The exact location of where to add this code can vary depending on your website, but generally, it goes in the body section just before the closing body tag. You can copy and paste the code for every website. For example, we installed the Simple Analytics script on the demo website using GitHub. intall-github.png Follow the steps, copy/paste the script and save it. If you look at the code you just copied, you can see the parts that indicate we are installing a custom domain. Also, we have enabled the Do Not Track feature in our settings, meaning it also collects those visits. The code does not work right away. You must first click “install the script” on the installation page. *(If you have a custom domain installed, scroll down to follow additional instructions)* After you click the button, it goes automatically, and we are almost ready! You must now wait for your first visit. install-website-loading.png You can visit your website yourself if you don’t see a recorded visit yet. Also, you can check if your website is properly sending data to Simple Analytics by visiting your website and inspect it. By opening the network tab and refreshing the page, you can see that the request is being sent to Simple Analytics. However, it's important to note that sometimes it may take a few minutes for a visit to be recorded, or the SSL certificate needs to be propagated, so the first visit may not be recorded well. We recommend waiting a few minutes before checking to ensure accurate data collection. If all is well, you should see something like this when returning to the installation page: install-dashboard.png There you go! Installing [Simple Analytics](https://simpleanalytics.com/) on your website is easy if you follow these four steps carefully. There are many advanced settings that you can tweak to meet your specific needs. ### DNS settings for Custom Domain If you have set up a custom domain, you must configure your DNS settings. You will need to add a name to your DNS that links to the external server that Simple Analytics provides. Here are the steps: To connect your subdomain to Simple Analytics, add a name to your DNS that matches your domain name. This subdomain must be linked to an external server hosted at *simpleanalyticsexternal.com* Everything you need to know about adding a custom domain can be found on [this page](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/bypass-ad-blockers). The process for adding this record to your DNS will vary depending on your DNS provider, but we will use Cloudflare as an example. Once you're in your Cloudflare account, you can add the record to link your subdomain to the Simple Analytics external server. It's important to note that the form for adding this record will look different for every provider, but the general steps will be the same. intall-dns-setting.png To link your custom domain to Simple Analytics, you first need to copy/paste the subdomain and select the ‘target’, which is: *simpleanalyticsexternal.com* and can be found [here](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/bypass-ad-blockers).  With Cloudflare, it's important to turn off the proxy because Simple Analytics installs the SSL certificate needed for a new custom domain. You can leave the time to live as automatic or set it to five minutes, which is usually enough as this domain is not changing many times. To ensure that the custom domain is properly set up and working, you can visit the domain and see if it loads correctly. If you encounter an SSL error, you can simply hit refresh in your website settings to resolve it. Checking the SSL can take a minute. Once it's done, it should be working fine. However, if you refresh your website and find that it's still not valid, it could be due to a cached SSL certificate in your browser or somewhere else on the network. [Please let us know](https://simpleanalytics.com/contact) if you still run into anything while installing Simple Analytics. ## GA4 is complex. Try Simple Analytics GA4 is like sitting in an airplane cockpit without a pilot license [Start for free now](/signup)

### Frequently Asked Questions.
What is the difference between the free trial and the POC?

The 14-day self-serve trial lets you explore Simple Analytics on your own. The free 30-day proof of concept is an assisted evaluation alongside GA4. Book a demo to discuss your measurement questions and agree on what to compare.

How does the 30-day proof of concept work?

First, we discuss your GA4 setup and define the measurement question you want answered. Next, you run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 for 30 days, keeping GA4 and your consent banner in place. We help optimize your Simple Analytics setup, including proxies and custom domains where needed. Finally, we review the differences together and assess whether Simple Analytics meets your reporting needs.

What will we compare during the proof of concept?

We agree on a measurement question for your website, such as differences in traffic volumes or campaign reporting. You run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 and compare the same dates and pages. We account for differences in metric definitions and implementation when interpreting the results.

What happens after the POC, and what will it cost?

We review the findings and discuss whether Simple Analytics fits your reporting needs. Enterprise pricing is quoted for your requirements. Discuss your expected traffic, sites, data access, and support needs on the demo so you can evaluate the commercial fit before deciding on a paid plan.

What we do and don't do with your data

The data we collect belongs to you. We only collect non-personal data, and we never sell it or share it with anyone for their own use. Your website data is stored in the EU, with our primary infrastructure in the Netherlands. It only goes to a provider outside the EU when you opt in to a feature that needs it, like the AI assistant.

What metrics do we collect?

We do not collect any personal data. We do not use cookies and never collect information that could be used to fingerprint a user. You do not need to tweak any settings to make our software privacy-friendly: Simple Analytics is privacy-friendly by design. Here is a [detailed list](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/what-we-collect) of what we do and don't collect from your visitors.

How does the free plan work?

Simple Analytics is free forever. To get started create an account to start your trial (no creditcard required). During 14-day trial you can explore all our features. After the 14 days, you'll need to select a plan to continue using Simple Analytics. You can choose to continue using one of our paid plans or downgrade to our free plan and continue using Simple Analytics free forever.

How does the 14-day self-serve trial work?

When you sign-up, your 14-day free trial (no credit card required) starts. No matter which plan you choose. During these 14 days, you can use advanced features without any restrictions. After the trial period, we'll ask you to choose a plan to continue using Simple Analytics. If you choose our paid plan, we need you to add your payment details. You can switch to any plan, provided your usage remains within its limits.

Is Simple Analytics GDPR-compliant?

Simple Analytics is GDPR compliant from installation. Because it only processes non-personal data, it can satisfy the requirements of the strictest privacy regulation, including the GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive, the UK GDPR, and the PECR. For more information [check our documentation](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/compliance).

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. You can cancel your subscription at any moment. You will still have access to your account and data until the end of the period you paid for.

What happens when your traffic grows?

You monthly fee will match your usage. Drag the slider to see what you pay for a certain amount of data points. Simple Analytics automatically calculates your data points (first looking back one month, then the average of the previous three months).

So, if you had an increase in traffic during the past three months, you pay only a little more next month. Likewise, you automatically pay a little less when your average amount of page views decreased during the last months.

How do we charge for yearly plans?

When you choose yearly, you estimate your traffic after your trial. We send you an email when you go over your limit, you have one week to increase your limit. Otherwise, we'll do it for you. To prevent extra invoices during the year, set your limit high enough. After the year, your datapoints will be reset to zero.

What does 30 day history mean?

You can use Simple Analytics for free forever (in our free plan). However, there are some limitations to this plan. One limit is on your analytics history, which is capped at 30 days. This means you can only view your website stats for the last 30 days. Any traffic data older than 30 days will be automatically deleted from our servers. If you need longer data history and retention, you can choose one of our paid plans.

What does unlimited pageviews mean?

Our free plan offers unlimited pageviews. This allows you to track as much traffic as your website gets without any restrictions. However, we have a fair use policy to make sure our servers run smoothly for all users. If your traffic exceeds our fair use limits, we'll notify you via email. If you're unsure about your website's traffic volume, feel free to [contact us](https://dashboard.simpleanalytics.com/contact) in advance.

What payment methods do you accept?

We accept Credit Card, Debit Card, Bitcoin +10% & yearly, Apple Pay, and Google Pay as payment methods for all our paid plans. You can pay in Euros, US Dollars or British Pounds. Bills from €500 can be paid via bank transfers and cost an additional 10% in banking and service fees.

[Start for free now](/signup)

Free forever  No credit card required  Cancel anytime

body.title: How VertoDigital plans a conversion check alongside GA4 - Simple Analytics
body.content:
Agency use case · VertoDigital

# A second view of the actions that matter to clients
VertoDigital is building a conversion measurement check with Simple Analytics alongside GA4. The question: how many demo requests, form submissions and downloads does each tool record?

[Book a demo](/demo)

One action. Two measurement paths.

Successful demo request

Example event definition

GA4

Existing collection and consent configuration

Simple Analytics

Independent cookieless event collection

Compare matching counts in Looker Studio

Proposed workflow. Shared triggers do not guarantee equal delivery or complete coverage.

## From an agency’s own site to a client playbook
VertoDigital works with B2B technology companies on marketing measurement and pipeline reporting. Its [Pipeline Intelligence offering](https://vertodigital.com/services/b2b-pipeline-intelligence-and-marketing-attribution) includes Simple Analytics alongside GA4, with a separate role for CRM integration and advertising activation.

The agency’s implementation brief starts on vertodigital.com. GA4, server-side Google Tag Manager, Usercentrics and Looker Studio are already part of the setup. Simple Analytics is installed for pageviews. The next step is to extend the comparison to the website actions the team reports as conversions.

This is a use case in development. The brief describes an internal reference implementation intended to inform client work; it does not yet establish a measured conversion gap or a completed client rollout.

## Pageviews are the starting point. Actions are the next question.
A visitor can reject analytics consent and still submit a form. If that action is absent from a report, an agency needs to establish whether the cause is consent configuration, event implementation or the report itself.

VertoDigital’s proposed comparison gives the analyst another count to investigate. It can help answer whether a change in reported conversions is also visible in an independent measurement source. It cannot, on its own, establish the number of unique leads or the amount of revenue a campaign generated.

The deliverable is a comparison the client can understand and the analyst can explain.

Which event was counted, what each tool received, and which differences remain unexplained.

### Define the same action in both tools
VertoDigital’s plan starts with an event map: GA4 names, triggers and parameters, matched to Simple Analytics events. Demo requests, form submissions, downloads and outbound contact clicks are in scope. Each has to mean the same thing in both reports.

### Separate the event from the consent check
The plan uses the same underlying website interaction to trigger both tags, while configuring their consent behavior separately. A shared trigger reduces definition drift; it does not guarantee that both tools receive the event. Script loading, delivery and duplicate firing still need checking.

### Compare counts in the client report
The proposed Looker Studio view puts matching event counts side by side over the same period. Pageview trends provide context. The aim is to give the client a repeatable measurement check, with each discrepancy investigated before it becomes a business conclusion.

Simple Analytics events must exclude personal data, including emails, hashed emails, user IDs and form-field contents. Review metadata and URLs too. Configure collection for the applicable requirements; do not copy GA4 consent settings into another tag without reviewing what that tag collects.

## Make the comparison defensible
Event definition
:   A successful form submission is different from clicking Submit. Use the same completion signal in both tools.

Counting method
:   Compare event occurrences with event occurrences. Do not assume a GA4 key-event total uses the same counting method.

Collection
:   Test accepted and rejected consent, script timing, failed requests, and automated versus custom events that could double-count an action.

Report scope
:   Align dates, time zones, sites and filters. Keep observed event counts distinct from modeled or attributed report metrics.

Denied consent does not always mean GA4 receives nothing. Basic Consent Mode blocks Google tags when consent is denied; advanced Consent Mode can send cookieless pings. Modeling is a separate reporting process with eligibility requirements. Check the actual configuration and report before interpreting a difference. [Google’s Consent Mode documentation](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/concepts/consent-mode) explains the distinction.

Simple Analytics can also miss events. A larger count is not a validation requirement, and a smaller one is a reason to investigate, not proof of a broken setup. Where available, check successful submissions against form-processing or CRM totals with matching scope, without sending those systems’ personal data to Simple Analytics.

## An independent check, with attribution kept in its place
In VertoDigital’s proposed setup, GA4 and BigQuery retain their existing role in attribution and CRM-related reporting. Simple Analytics supplies a separate view of recorded website actions. Its counts do not identify missing individuals or automatically feed additional conversions into bidding algorithms.

Keep the two sources side by side, or aggregate them to a common reporting grain before joining. Do not join them on user or session identifiers, and do not add their totals together: both tools may have recorded the same action.

[How Simple Analytics records events →](https://docs.simpleanalytics.com/events)[How Simple Analytics measures without visitor identities →](/sessions-without-consent)

## Are your conversion counts telling the same story?
Run Simple Analytics alongside GA4 in a free 30-day proof of concept. We’ll help you compare the same website actions, check the setup and understand why the counts differ.

[Book a demo](/demo)

Keep GA4 and your consent banner in place.

body.title: Features - Simple Analytics
body.content:
# What you can do with Simple Analytics
Understand your website traffic **without losing data** or violating your visitors' privacy. Simple Analytics gives you three core capabilities:

### Understand your traffic
See where visitors come from and how they browse your site, even when they reject consent.

### Track what matters
Monitor the events and goals that drive your business.

### Use your data anywhere
Export, embed, or get reports delivered to your inbox.

### Filters
